questions.question: What is an offtake agreement in mining and why do lenders want one?

facts: a contract in which a buyer agrees to purchase a stated share of future production, often at a set or formula price
lenders use it as evidence of future revenue that supports project finance
it can include price floors, ceilings or volume commitments and affects project risk
truth.tolerance: the key points must be present and correct; extra correct detail is fine
truth.source: general knowledge, written before any system was asked

questions.question: What is the difference between a scoping study, a pre-feasibility study and a definitive feasibility study?

facts: they are successive study levels with increasing accuracy and cost, from scoping (lowest confidence) to pre-feasibility to definitive feasibility
a definitive or bankable feasibility study supports a final investment decision and financing
the accuracy of cost estimates improves at each stage, for example from roughly +/-30-50% to +/-10-15%
truth.tolerance: the key points must be present and correct; extra correct detail is fine
truth.source: general knowledge, written before any system was asked

questions.question: Why do analysts worry when one country produces most of a critical mineral?

importers have few alternative suppliers, so shocks transmit directly to prices and availability
diversification, stockpiling, recycling and new mines are common policy responses
